scope: Perspective correction plus provincial governor's court
prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: transparent modular architecture atlas for a distant pixel-illustrated dark-fantasy strategy map.
Edit/rebuild the FIRST reference atlas into a new 4-column by 3-row sheet containing EXACTLY TWELVE complete isolated architectural components with generous transparent gutters. The first eight cells replace its eight capital sections; the last four add parts of a lower fortified provincial governor's hall and gate court. No labels or cell lines. This is a PARTS ATLAS, never one painting of a whole city or region.

Input roles: image 1 is the existing capital design to revise; retain its Warlord identity, materials, seven-section ascending citadel concept and approximate overall architectural extent. Its near-frontal camera is REJECTED. Image 2 is the surrounding small-building kit: use its door/window/world scale and its visible roofs and two side faces as the minimum perspective depth.

PRIMARY CORRECTION: redraw ALL twelve objects from one consistent HIGH, DIAGONAL THREE-QUARTER OVERHEAD camera: look down from the southeast, about 45 degrees above the ground, with the long architectural axis receding toward upper-left. See broad roof planes, terrace floors, parapet thickness, courtyard depth and TWO clearly different wall faces. An off-centre corner faces the viewer. No frontal symmetrical elevation, no straight horizontal wall strip, no orthographic front view. Do not simply skew or rotate flat sprites. These are genuinely volumetric buildings with lit tops, quieter fronts and a darker side plane. All parts share identical projection and upper-left lighting. Keep small doors/windows: major walls have MANY ordinary storeys/bays, never one gigantic entrance. The capital remains monumental because it contains more architecture; do not enlarge individual building details.

Style: deliberate hard pixel clusters, broad readable connected material/value groups, selective dithering, restrained highlights; painterly old-school dark fantasy translated to small map sprites. No glossy mobile-game render or soft blur. Inhabited imperial construction. Muted slate masonry, vermilion/brick-red tiled roofs and narrow cloth, oxidized teal structural binding. Ossified ribs and spine braces are actual load-bearing masonry/vaults, not loose skeleton decoration. Keep usable stairs, entrances and courts clear. Capital summit: THREE rigid spear-prong towers joined by ONE closed teal band. Provinces echo severe rib-braced construction without copying that tall triple-prong summit. No skull faces, readable faces, people, writing, UI or pasted faction crest. Structural decay is restrained at outer edges.

Exact row-major cells, each one a COMPLETE module with no ground plate or landscape:
1. Capital lower central gate terrace: broad retaining bastion with a usable SMALL entrance, visible deep stair/terrace floor and diagonal returns. Base section only.
2. Capital lower-left terrace wing: curved return wall and red-roof gallery, ample visible floor/roof depth, open construction end to overlap cell 1.
3. Capital lower-right terrace wing: complementary right-hand return, same elevation and camera.
4. Capital rear buttress section: connected piers and rib-built vault supports, visible tops, a low rear support for the stack. No mountain or rock backdrop.
5. Capital middle terrace collar: shallow U-shaped fortified court with clearly visible floor and red-roof rear galleries; diagonal, not front-on. Only this level.
6. Capital upper palace: connected long hall and short lateral wings, many tiny ordinary windows, strong roof planes and receding side face, footprint attaches above cell 5. Not a whole castle.
7. Capital summit: the three narrow, tall rigid stone spear-prongs with one shared teal bridge-band; visible tower roof/upper ledges and side planes, no lower fortress.
8. Broken low outer stepped rampart and access stair, same diagonal projection.
9. Provincial governor's hall: LOWER and BROADER silhouette, long red-roof administrative/assembly hall, attached small side wing, two squat rib-braced corner bastions and a usable ordinary entrance. No crown-spire summit. ONE major hall section, not an entire city or walled compound.
10. Provincial gatehouse: low paired rectangular gate towers with a roofed bridge and SMALL passage, a short diagonal wall return on each side, compatible with the hall.
11. Provincial gate court: architectural paving enclosed on TWO sides by a low arcade and parapet, open joining ends; a readable shallow court, no rectangular terrain tile.
12. Provincial side gallery: low L-shaped red-roof wing with a short stair and rib-built supports, joins the hall and court.

Every part fully visible and isolated with true alpha transparency around it; all tall tips and wall ends inside their cell. No decorative vignette, scenic background, city surrounding any part, map polygon, terrain panel, cast shadow rectangle, fog, glow or labels. Leave joining ends as masonry construction interfaces. Do not paint a complete region-sized building/city.
